title: DependencyGraph
description: Standard input format for the NTM-BP engine. A directed fact-dependency graph whose nodes are fact IDs and whose edges carry optional Conditional Probability Tables (CPTs) and an optional relation-type tag. This is the interchange format consumed by ntm_bp.graph.DependencyGraph.from_dict() and produced by to_dict(). Any RAG / agent-memory system can emit this format to plug its own fact graph into NTM-BP.

nodes.description: Fact IDs present in the graph (may be empty if edges alone define all nodes; add_edge auto-registers endpoints).

edges.description: Directed dependency edges: edge (parent, child) means 'child depends on parent'; a change in the parent's value should decay the child's belief.

relation_type.description: Semantic tag for the edge. Only consumed by the experimental CO engine (gamma multipliers 1.2 / 1.3 / 0.5 / 1.0); the core NTM-BP engine ignores it. 'default' means standard NTM-BP propagation.

cpt.description: Conditional Probability Table for the edge: cpt[parent_value][child_value] = P(child_value | parent_value). Probabilities must be in [0, 1]; rows need not sum to 1. Missing keys fall back to the uniform default 0.5 at query time.

parent.description: Premise fact ID (must exist in 'nodes' or be added implicitly).

child.description: Conclusion fact ID that depends on the parent.

scenario.description: Full evaluation scenario used by the benchmark scripts (PC-500 / SynDep). A scenario embeds a DependencyGraph plus an update instruction and the manually annotated ground truth. Emitting scenarios in this format lets the community evaluate their own graphs against the paper's metrics.

facts.description: Initial fact values and confidences: fact_id -> [value, confidence].

ground_truth_reeval.description: Manually annotated set of fact IDs that semantically require re-evaluation (algorithm-independent; may be empty).

theta.description: Annotated semantic impact strength in [0, 1] (NOT derived from 1 - new_confidence).

relation_types.description: Edge relation tags. Either a dict {"parent__child": "supports"} or a list [["parent", "child", "supports"]].
